title: Number Patterns
description: Identifying sequences and finding rules using nth term formulas.

notes.heading: Arithmetic Sequences
notes.body: A sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is constant (common difference d). Example: 3,7,11,15,... has d=4. nth term: a+(n−1)d, where a is the first term.

notes.heading: The nth Term Formula
notes.body: For arithmetic sequences: T(n)=dn+c where d=common difference. Example: 5,8,11,14,... → d=3, T(n)=3n+2. Check: n=2 gives 3(2)+2=8 ✓.

notes.heading: Other Patterns
notes.body: Geometric: multiply by a fixed ratio (2,6,18,54,... r=3). Square numbers: 1,4,9,16,25,... Triangular numbers: 1,3,6,10,15,... Check differences — if first differences constant = arithmetic; second differences constant = n² term.

flashcards.definition: Fixed amount added each term in an arithmetic sequence.
Formula giving value of any term by its position n.
Each term multiplied by a fixed ratio.
Numbers from multiplying a whole number by itself: 1,4,9,16,25,...
